note: SELF-008 install self package: the claim is that install and jckgx run through the same verification path, and src/selfhost/install.zig makes that a literal property of the code - one verify function decides, and both entry points call it. The test asserts it behaviourally rather than structurally: a tampered package is refused by both entry points with the same error, an untrusted channel is refused by both before any bytes are considered, and a good package produces the identical verified identity through both. The trust root is an input, never implied by the channel: a channel that could assert its own trustworthiness would be no channel at all. Fault proof: giving the runner its own trustworthiness check makes the tampered-package refusal fail on that path (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain. Scope note, stated plainly: this case evidences the shared verification path; wiring the CLI's install command and the jckgx binary onto it is the remaining self-hosting work, and the binary's root convention is defined by that install command rather than invented ahead of it.
authority: self-reported local review, not independent attestation
